1451.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tʰunkʰanō, from the nasal-infixed present *dʰu-n-gʰ- of Proto-Indo-European *dʰewgʰ- (“to hit, produce, yield”), whence also τεύχω (teúkhō, “produce”).

1495.t: From Proto-Hellenic *erutʰrós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rudʰrós (“red”), from the root *h₁rewdʰ-. Compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀬𐀲𐀨 (e-ru-ta-ra).

1403.t: Disputed. * Possibly from a Mediterranean substrate; compare Old Armenian անթայր (antʻayr, “spark; anthrax”), անթեղ (antʻeł, “hot coal, ember”).

1485.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʰehliyoi, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰesliyoy, from *ǵʰes-, whence χείρ (kheír)), as if meaning “full hand”. Cognates include Sanskrit सहस्र (sahásra) and Latin mīlle.

1425.t: From Proto-Hellenic *téktōn, from Proto-Indo-European *tétḱō (“carpenter”), from *tetḱ- (“to create, produce”). Cognate with Sanskrit तक्षन् (tákṣan).

1454.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵr̥yos (“campestral, of a field”). By surface analysis, ἀγρός (agrós, “field, country”) + -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix).

1424.t: From τράγω (trágō, “to gnaw, nibble”) + -ος (-os, “nominal suffix”), literally “gnawer, eater (of sweets)”.

1469.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kapnós, from Proto-Indo-European *kwep- (“to smoke, boil, move violently”), which appears to be a European substrate word; see also Lithuanian kūpėti (“to boil over”), Old Church Slavonic кꙑпѣти (kypěti, “to boil”), Sanskrit कुप्यति…

1437.t: From βάσανος (básanos, “touchstone”) + -ίζω (-ízō, “verbal suffix”), literally “to test with touchstone”.

1407.t: Possibly from Proto-Hellenic *ewajō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁wéh₂-ye-ti, from the root *h₁weh₂- (“to leave, abandon”). However, the augment of the Classical Greek preterite points to Proto-Hellenic *hewajō.

1456.t: From Proto-Hellenic *eléutʰeros, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁léwdʰeros, from *h₁lewdʰ- (“to grow up; people, tribe”); the original meaning of the word was "belonging to the tribe".

1478.t: From Proto-Hellenic *plā́t͏̌t͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *pl(e)h₂kyeti, from *pleh₂k-, *pleh₂g- (“to strike”).

1415.t: From Proto-Hellenic *nekʷʰrós, from Proto-Indo-European *negʷʰrós. Cognates include Latin nefrōnes and Proto-Germanic *neurô.

1473.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ḱélh₂m̥ (“reed, straw”) via its zero-grade stem (such as genitive *ḱl̥h₂mós, with a shift in accent to *ḱĺ̥h₂mos), or (according to Beekes) independently thematicized from an original ablauting paradigm *ḱólh₂-m̥ ~ *ḱl̥h₂-ém-.

1400.t: Apparently from a Proto-Indo-European *h₂rh₁téh₂, from a root *h₂erh₁- (“to arrange, fit”).

1480.t: From Proto-Indo-European *peh₂ǵ- (“to coagulate, become fixed”). Cognates include Latin pangō and Old English fōn (English fang).

1484.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *kʷelh₁- Proto-Hellenic *kʷélos Ancient Greek τέλος (télos) Proto-Indo-European *-yoh₂ Proto-Hellenic *-yō Ancient Greek *-ϳω (*-jō) Ancient Greek τελέω From τέλος (télos, “end”) + *-ϳω (*-jō, denominative verbal suffix).

1435.t: From Proto-Indo-European *oktōḱomt, from earlier *oḱto(w)-dḱomt (“eight-ten”), influenced by ὀγδόη (ogdóē) in analogy with ἑβδομήκοντα (hebdomḗkonta). Cognate with Latin octōgintā, Old Armenian ութսուն (utʻsun).

1431.t: For the “shield” sense, traditionally derived from ἀ- (a-) + σπίζω (spízō, “to extend”).

1409.t: Uncertain. Beekes states a formation in *-nos- like ἔρνος (érnos), κτῆνος (ktênos).

1439.t: Apparently from a Proto-Hellenic *klə́dos, from Proto-Indo-European *kl̥d-o-s (“piece of wood”), which is traditionally linked to *kelh₂- (“to break”).

1477.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ped͏̌d͏̌ós, from Proto-Indo-European *ped-yo-s (“foot”); see also πούς (poús).

1438.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kārūt͏̌t͏̌ō. By surface analysis, κήρυκ- (kḗrūk-, stem of κῆρυξ (kêrŭx)) + *-ϳω (*-jō).

1419.t: The first component of the word is likely from Proto-Indo-European *pres (“before, in front”), an extended form of *per-.

1481.t: The word has been connected with σκύλαξ (skúlax, “puppy”), but the variation of the suffix remains unclear on this account. The suffix "-μν-" could point to a Pre-Greek origin.

1496.t: From ἑκατόν (hekatón, “one hundred”) + -στός (-stós), a variant of -τός (-tós, ordinal suffix).

1476.t: παῖς (paîs) + *-ϳω (*-jō), i.e. "to act like a child" > "to play".

1466.t: Univerbation of δι’ ὅ (di’ hó); see διά (dĭắ, “because of”) and ὅ (hó, “which”).

1441.t: Possibly a Pre-Greek word; see also Semitic: Akkadian 𒄢 (kalû /⁠GUL⁠/, “to detain, delay, hold back [a person], to keep in custody, in confinement, to distrain, to prevent, to hinder”) Biblical Hebrew כֶּלֶא (kéle, “prison, jail”), Aramaic כלא (kəlāʾ, “to…

1452.t: From χίλιοι (khílioi, “thousand”) + ἄρχω (árkhō, “to rule”). Calque of Old Persian *hazahrapatiš.

1472.t: From Proto-Hellenic *klāyyō, from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂uyeti, from *kleh₂u- (“hook, key”), whence κληΐς (klēḯs), κλήϊθρον (klḗïthron).

1467.t: Reanalyzed as a -μα-stem from Epic δῶ (dô), from Proto-Indo-European *dṓm (“home; house”). Compare δόμος (dómos), δεσπότης (despótēs).

1436.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₃r̥dʰ-ro-, from *h₃erdʰ- (“to rise”). Cognate with ὀρθός (orthós), Latin ortus (“star's rise”), oriens (“sunrise”).

1432.t: From ἀ- (a-, alpha privative) + τιμή (tīmḗ, “honour”) + -άζω (-ázō, denominative verb suffix).

1410.t: Variant of ἵλαος (hī́laos, “auspicious, favorable”) formed after the pattern ναός (nāós) : νεώς (neṓs), λαός (lāós) : λεώς (leṓs).

1458.t: From ἐν- (en-, “there”) + τοῦ (toû, “(medial)”) + -θεν (-then, “from”). For another modification to τοῦ (toû), see οὗτος (hoûtos).

1488.t: From ἀ- (a-, negation prefix) + βατός (bătós, “passable; accessible”).

1422.t: From σκῦλα (skûlă, “war booty”), the latter according to Beekes, from σκύλλω (skúllō, “to flay”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kelH- (“to cut”).

1446.t: From στένω (sténō, “to moan, lament”) + -άζω (-ázō, frequentative suffix).

1411.t: From Biblical Hebrew יְהוֹיָקִים (Yəhôyāqîm, literally “raised by the Lord”).

1413.t: From κατα- (kata-, back, down) + ἥκω (hḗkō, “to have come, be present”).

1493.t: Etymology tree Ancient Greek ἐνθυμέομαι (enthuméomai) Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥ Proto-Hellenic *-mə Ancient Greek -μα (-ma) Ancient Greek ἐνθύμημα From ἐνθυμέομαι (enthuméomai, “infer, conclude”) + -μα (-ma)
